title: AI Drives Global Goods Trade Facing Trump Tariffs, War Headwinds
source_used: The Economic Times (summary of a DHL-Stern report citing WTO and OECD data)
key_facts: Global goods trade is projected to grow significantly this year, driven primarily by demand for AI products.
Merchandise trade growth is expected to reach 4.6% this year, despite tariffs and geopolitical tensions (DHL-Stern report).
AI-enabling goods accounted for 42% of all merchandise trade growth last year.
That share jumped to nearly 76% during the first quarter of 2026.
The figures cite WTO and OECD data.
quote_evidence: AI-enabling goods accounted for 42% of all merchandise trade growth last year, a share that jumped to nearly 76% during the first quarter of 2026, the report said, citing WTO and OECD data.
Global goods trade is projected to grow significantly this year, driven primarily by demand for artificial intelligence products.
why_it_matters_hint: AI hardware now drives most of the trade growth, though the 4.6% is a forecast from one report.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (HTTP 403). Read on The Economic Times, which summarises the DHL-Stern report and its WTO/OECD data. The DHL-Stern report itself was not opened; its figures are used as ET gives them.
